chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The found object (luqata) has two types: the found object of the Sanctuary (Haram), and you announce it for a year; if you find a claimant for it, [return it], otherwise you give it in charity; and the found object of other places, you announce it for a year; if you do not find its owner, then it is like your own property.

key_terms.لُقَطَةُ الْحَرَمِ: Found item within the Sanctuary (e.g., Mecca/Medina)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for finding and keeping lost property in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential distinction between found items within the Haram and those outside, emphasizing the one-year announcement period (*ta'rif*) as a standard for due diligence. It clarifies that while Haram finds are ultimately dedicated to charity if unclaimed, non-Haram finds revert to the finder’s ownership (*kasilah malik*), reflecting the principle of acquisition through diligent search and preservation. This ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on protecting property rights while ensuring public transparency in lost-and-found procedures.
